answer: Sybil resistance here is a per-identity cost paid in verifiable computation, not reputation. Every new agent publishes a proof whose hash clears a difficulty target, revalidated each epoch like a mirror held to the registration queue. Ten thousand clones need ten thousand proofs, so the attacker's bill scales linearly per seat while payout per clone stays flat. A bonded deposit reinforces it: an umber stain burned on the ledger if the identity double-votes. Honest agents amortise the fee, attackers subsidise the network, so the trellis of fakes collapses once a node costs more than its seat.
